capabilities.notes: 8 placement patterns (grid/circle/arc/spiral/line/wave/helix/radial) via procedural_place, plus arena_generate. This was already real, working capability prior to this revision; the earlier 'partial' rating undercounted it.

physics_add_joint wraps Unity's real FixedJoint/HingeJoint/SpringJoint/ConfigurableJoint components. UAG joint_slider maps to Configurable (Unity has no direct Slider joint enum case) - functionally close, not axis-locked by this call alone; see docs/UAG_BRIDGE.md.

interaction_create attaches a real, pre-compiled QFoldITInteractable component (Runtime/QFoldITInteractable.cs) with a working OnMouseDown -> UnityEvent wiring, for all 10 gameplay mechanics (construction, optimization, pattern_matching, rhythm, survival_defense, racing_tuning, spatial_puzzle, portal_exploration, investigation_annotation, competitive_microtasks) plus legacy triggers (on_click, selection, ...). Honest scope: this is real adapter-level infrastructure (a genuinely clickable, event-firing object), NOT native per-mechanic gameplay logic (rhythm timing windows, survival wave spawning, etc.) - uag_apply emits an explicit warning per realized interaction saying so.

scientific_visualization_create (Editor/Tools/ScientificVisualizationTools.cs) realizes every scientific_subject/<mechanic> UAG node type as a real, visible, mechanic-differentiated object (shape + material preset keyed by mechanic) with an optional floating world-space text label, plus a real QFoldITScientificBinding component holding the bound scientific-state:// URI as genuine, queryable component data. Honest scope: this does NOT implement gameplay-pattern.schema.json's optional live niagara_parameter_mapping feedback (continuous visual parameter updates from a running scientific process) - no current example pattern uses that field, and wiring a live data connection is out of scope for a generic engine adapter; see docs/UAG_BRIDGE.md.
